title: enterprise bundle anchors install --json (Linux, macOS)
description: `enterprise bundle anchors install --file F [--lock-wait D] --json` on Linux and macOS. The verb is not registered on Windows, where the call is `enterprise windows ensure --profile standalone --trust-anchors F [--bundle B] --json` and prints lifecycle result v2. Source trust: the verb reads F once, as LoadAnchors(F, TrustAnchorFile) does (internal/enterprisebundle/anchors.go): Lstat, regular file, the file and every folder above it root-owned, not group or other writable, without an ACL write entry and without links; open; SameFile against the Lstat; bounded read; strict decode. A source that fails is refused (anchor_insecure, anchor_missing or anchor_invalid) and nothing is written. The bytes written are exactly the bytes validated in that one read. Then, under the lifecycle lock: a file byte-identical to a trusted installed file is result unchanged and writes nothing; otherwise <etc>/trust/bundle-anchors.json is written atomically (root:root 0644 in a root 0755 folder) and re-checked with TrustAnchorFile, and the previous file is put back when that check fails. From 1.0.4 every install that changes the file, is refused or fails leaves a change event that the gateway reports, when it runs, as one config.trust_anchors.changed audit and OTel event (hashes and key ids only); builds before 1.0.4 record none. An install whose change event cannot be recorded is refused (state_invalid) before the file is written. The result still carries sha256, previous_sha256 and key_ids for the agent's own report. Exit codes: 0; 1 refused (errors[0].code); 2 invalid arguments; 75 lifecycle_busy.

result.description: installed: no anchor file before (bundle mode turns on); replaced: the installed file was replaced (a different file, or identical bytes in an installed file that failed its trust check, then previous_sha256 equals sha256); unchanged: byte-identical, nothing written; refused: nothing written, the previous file (if any) stays.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file now installed (absent when refused and none is installed).

previous_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file replaced (result replaced).

key_ids.description: key_id of every key in the installed file, in file order.

warnings.description: The codes bundleCurrentSignerWarning emits (internal/cli/enterprise_bundle_status.go), checked against the new file: key_unknown (the confirmed bundle's signer is not in it), key_revoked (it is revoked there), anchor_unreadable. The current bundle keeps enforcing; the next bundle must be signed by an active key. change_unrecorded: the change event of this run could not be written, so the gateway will not report it. change_release_unflushed: the run changed nothing, but the room it reserved for its change event could not be removed durably, so after a power loss the gateway may report it as an interrupted change.

errors.description: Codes: anchor_insecure (the source file or a folder above it can be written by a non-root account, is a link, or changed while it was read; or the installed file failed the re-check), anchor_missing (--file does not exist), anchor_invalid, anchor_restore_failed, lifecycle_busy, not_managed, not_supported_secure_client, state_invalid, not_root, invalid_arguments.

errors.message: bundle anchor_invalid: bundle-anchors.json: keys[0].not_after: want an RFC 3339 UTC time ending in Z
bundle anchor_insecure: bundle-anchors.json: /var/lib/acme-agent/trust is writable by group or other accounts

warnings.message: the confirmed bundle's signer acme-2026a is revoked in the installed trust anchors; it keeps enforcing until a bundle signed by an active key replaces it
